steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Stir in rotini and return to a boil. Cook pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain and rinse with cold water; set aside.
Whisk mayonnaise, vinegar, garlic, salt, and black pepper together in a large bowl until combined. Stir in basil.
Stir in rotini, tomatoes, bell pepper, and olives gently until combined. Chill in the refrigerator for 3 hours to overnight. Stir gently before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Italian Confetti Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This tri-colored rotini pasta salad recipe with mayonnaise includes fresh tomatoes, bell pepper, and basil with olives, rotini, and a creamy dressing.

review.reviewBody: WARNING: DO NOT USE LOW FAT MAYONNAISE. I made it the first time with regular mayonnaise and it turned out to be the hit of the party! I couldn't find fresh basil so I even used dried. Then I decided to make it with low fat mayonnaise and it turned out horrible. Great recipe...

A little variation: Add red, orange and yellow bell pepper, diced; a can of drained pineapple chunks OR a cup of small seedless red grapes, halved. This adds a little sweet touch to the savory and despite how odd it sounds, is very good. 

Black olives, sliced green olives with pimentos, diced sauteed or fresh zucchini or yellow squash... This is a versatile, easy and festive side dish for a large gathering.

This is one of the easiest and most delicious sides I've ever made. It's perfect because you can do all of the prep work ahead of time (dicing/slicing veggies and boiling pasta) and then just mix them all together when you're ready to eat. 

I did make one big change to the recipe. I didn't use any mayonnaise. I wanted something lighter to go along with the salmon I was cooking and I felt the mayonnaise would be too heavy. I am SO glad that I didn't! The red wine vinegar alone is more than enough to give this a delicious taste. Plus, it makes the freshly cut veggies stand out. I have made this probably 2 dozen times now and I love it every time!

One tip, once your pasta is done boiling and you've strained it, add the red wine vinegar immediately. This will prevent the pasta from sticking together while it sits to cool down. Trying to add it once it's cooled down is a nightmare.

This was an easy pasta salad, one of my coworkers made it for an employee luncheon and I wanted to tried it she gave me the link to the recipe. I use yellow bell peppers, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and onions. I added season salt, pepper, garlic powder, crush red peppers and a little bit of sriracha sauce. I miss all the seasoning in the mayo mixture before adding the pasta and veggies, from reading the recipe I reduce the mayo and did add a little bit of sour cream, then sprinkle some can corn on top. My husband who's not a big fan of pasta salad loved it, I would make it again for my household and for events. I did not give it a five star because if I followed the recipe exact it would have been too much mayo and not enough flavor.

chop and DRAIN tomatoes, or use cherry tomatoes. 
I used gently roaster cherry tomatoes and allowed them to cool. Added a full new dimension of flavor that complimented all of the ingredients.
I added feta cheese, blanched broccoli and I also seasoned the pasta after I cooked it w garlic powder and onion powder salt pepper. Delicious!

This was a wonderful, quick and easy pasta salad. LOW-Fat mayo is great. 

I used blanched broccoli and tomatoes as my vegetables. I've made it like this twice, using bowtie pasta (my favourite) and served it on the same day as well as the day after. Both quite delicious.

I used scoobi doo noodles for this :). I used part mayo and part sour cream to make up the 1 cup - i just didn't want to use that much mayo. some others said it was too much dressing on the pasta - but i was making mine a day in advance and since i find homemade pasta salad tends to absorb the dressing and dry out a bit when left in the fridge overnight, i left the measurements as is and it was perfect for me by the next day. I left out the olives and basil only as a preference - and I added chives, cucumber, celery and used red pepper instead of yellow because that's what I had. I think I'd make it again with my own variations. Oh and i cut the salt in half :)

This was my first attempt at pasta salad! My salad turned out pretty good, but 1 tblsp of salt is a bit too much. Would definitely suggest using half the amount then tasting; add more if necessary. Lots of sauce, would also recommend 1 cup more of dried pasta.

 I ended up using a half cup mayo, and a half cup of low fat whipped dressing. I substituted balsamic vinegar for red wine vinegar, dried basil (1tblsp), black garlic (just because I had some) and added a bit of diced red onion and diced dill pickles, and no olives (didn't have any).

As much as I love mayonnaise (and I really do!), 1 cup of mayo for only two cups of pasta was way too much for me. I ended up cooking the entire (12 oz.) box of pasta (about 4 1/2 cups uncooked) and just added more veggies to match the ratio. Didn't have fresh basil so I just added 2 tsp. dried basil to the mayo mixture. The flavor of the sauce is fabulous! Will definitely make this again!

Great base recipe...although I made several alterations. I cut the mayo down to about 1/8 cup, as we're not huge fans of anything overly creamy. I also soaked raw, red onions in a 1/4 cup of sherry vinegar, which was added to the pasta mixture, along with blanched asparagus & broccoli, goat cheese, pan fried prosciutto, cherry tomatoes, and olives. Wonderful!
Made this with Vegenaise and it was great. I will be adding this to my rotation.

In reading the reviews I saw that everyone changed the ingredients, added to or subtracted from, and everyone loved their results! I had to substitute to tricolor trottole pasta only because my grocery store carried no other tricolored pasta, and I wanted that fun of color. When I do it again I’ll use half the sauce or else double the pasta, as there is too much sauce, which the photo does not show! Loved it and will make it again; it is a great basic recipe.
Can’t get enough of this pasta salad! Fresh basil makes all the difference.
I added salami and cheese cubes.

Tried the recipe as discribed and loved it however the second go around, I added some celery, pimento and avocado, replaced the basil with cilantro and cubes of smoked brisket with a pinch of italian dressing without the mayo. All gone...
